reason: The text demonstrates that non-leaders exercise agency alongside leaders. While Moses and Aaron receive direct commands from God, the passage explicitly describes the broader Israelite population performing independent actions: they carry their unleavened dough (וַיִּשָּׂ֥א הָעָ֛ם), they ask the Egyptians for items (וַֽיִּשְׁאֲלוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם), and they bake bread (וַיֹּאפ֨וּ). The Egyptians also demonstrate agency by willingly providing these items (וַיַּשְׁאִל֑וּם). The phrase 'כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל' (all the children of Israel) performing these actions shows agency distributed throughout the community, not concentrated solely in leadership.
